summary: A point in a national or state address usually opens on a claim, not on context.
realLife: 44% of 175 coded points opened on a claim: 47% in inaugurals, 41% in State of the State addresses.
sources: docs/story/research/address-moves.md (Elections lane, Nov 24, 2026: 6 inaugurals and 6 State of the State addresses read whole, 175 points coded)
inGame: Outline moves `creed`, `stand` and `today` open a theme point (data/english/outlines.json shapes creed-then-pledge, today-then-stand); the claim is the speaker's belief or stance record on the policy question.

turns.what: The point opens on context or a fact before any claim, as a State of the State budget point does.
turns.pulledBy: a speaker high in analytical or meticulous; a point with a measure to cite (context-years, context-name)
turns.writesBack: The listener hears the claim later; the news story quotes the fact, not the claim.

turns.what: The claim comes only after a callback to the speech's own earlier words.
turns.pulledBy: the point follows a point already said (told-theme)
turns.writesBack: The earlier line gets said twice, so it must be one the speaker wants repeated.
